An initialised AVBPrint, borrowed mutably for the call: when len is non-zero, writes *str = 0 and len = 0 (storage, size and size_max kept; a truncated buffer becomes complete). *str is always writable: str is the inline storage for a count-only buffer (size 0), else size >= 1.

An initialised AVBPrint (av_bprint_init / av_bprint_init_for_buffer), borrowed mutably for the call only and not retained. Appends the escaped text through av_bprint_chars / av_bprintf (see their growth and truncation).
Extra characters backslash mode escapes, read with strchr for the call only; NULL means none (`special_chars &&`). Ignored by the quote and XML modes.
Text to escape, read up to its NUL for the call only. Must not be NULL, and must not point into dstbuf's storage (appends may realloc it).

The AVBPrint being finalized, borrowed: its heap str (when av_bprint_is_allocated) is av_freep'd when ret_str is NULL, or handed to *ret_str and buf->str cleared; buf->size is set to the final size. The struct's own storage is kept (caller-provided).

Optional out slot for the string, an alloc-constructor output (av_free releases it): the shrunk av_realloc heap buffer (or the unshrunk one when that realloc fails), else av_memdup(buf->str, min(len + 1, size)) for an internal/user buffer, NULL with AVERROR(ENOMEM) when that copy fails. NULL slot discards the string. C DEFECT: for an AV_BPRINT_SIZE_COUNT_ONLY buffer (av_bprint_init(.., 0, AV_BPRINT_SIZE_COUNT_ONLY), or av_bprint_init_for_buffer with size 0) size is 0, so the result is av_memdup(str, 0) = a 1-byte av_malloc block that is never written: NOT NUL-terminated (ASan: heap-buffer-overflow in strlen). A wrapper must not adopt that result as an owned string (HeapString). The lifecycle role below is the AVBPrint teardown; the string output is recorded here because the schema carries one role per symbol.

Out slot, written unconditionally: the room size - min(len, size) after any growth, which may be smaller (limit, ENOMEM, truncated buffer) or larger than size; it includes the byte the NUL must keep. Must not be NULL.

An initialised AVBPrint, borrowed mutably: when size > room it calls av_bprint_alloc(buf, size) (same growth rules as the appenders, failure ignored); len is NOT changed: the caller commits what it wrote by raising len and re-terminating (pngdec.c: bp->len += n; bp->str[bp->len] = 0).

Out slot, written unconditionally: str + len, a borrow into buf's string storage (inline storage, owned av_realloc block or caller buffer), valid for *actual_size bytes of writes until the next append, finalize or move of buf; NULL when the room is 0. Bytes past str[len] are uninitialised (av_realloc), str[len] holds the NUL. Must not be NULL.

Caller storage of one AVBPrint, written in place without being read: str = reserved_internal_buffer, len = 0, size = min(automatic size, size_max), size_max (1 replaced by the automatic size), *str = 0; then av_bprint_alloc grows into an av_realloc block when size_init exceeds the inline size (silently keeping the inline buffer on failure). The struct must not move afterwards (str points into it).

Caller storage of one AVBPrint, initialised in place: str = buffer, len = 0, size = size_max = size, *str = 0; with size 0 it delegates to av_bprint_init(buf, 0, AV_BPRINT_SIZE_COUNT_ONLY) (inline, count only).

A caller byte buffer of `size` chars that the AVBPrint stores in str and writes for its whole life (never reallocated: size == size_max makes av_bprint_alloc fail with EIO); it must outlive the AVBPrint and must never reach av_bprint_finalize, which would av_realloc/av_free it since str != reserved_internal_buffer. Not dereferenced when size is 0, so NULL is accepted then.
An initialised AVBPrint, read for the call only (len < size); static inline in bprint.h.

An initialised AVBPrint (av_bprint_init / av_bprint_init_for_buffer), borrowed mutably for the call only and not retained. A new sole, writable reference to size av_malloc'd bytes, UNINITIALISED, freed with av_buffer_default_free (av_free) when the last reference goes; NULL when av_malloc fails (above av_max_alloc) or the AVBuffer/AVBufferRef allocation fails (data freed then). Rust: BufferReference::alloc -> UninitBuffer, a hand-written owner exposing &mut [MaybeUninit<u8>] until fill/copy_from_slice/assume_init.

av_buffer_alloc(size) then memset(data, 0, size): a new sole, writable reference to size zeroed av_malloc bytes, released by av_buffer_unref; NULL on failure. Rust: BufferReference::alloc_zeroed -> BufferReferenceBox.

size bytes whose ownership moves to the new AVBuffer on success (released by free(opaque, data), or av_free when free is NULL); untouched on failure (NULL return). Never dereferenced by av_buffer_create itself; NULL is stored as is (fine with size 0). Writes go through it later only while the reference is writable, so READONLY data is never written by C. Rust: a HeapVec<u8> (default free) or the slice of a boxed Rust owner T: AsMut<[u8]>/AsRef<[u8]> (+ Send + 'static).

Rust: NULL for HeapVec data, or release_owner::<T> (drops the Box<T> passed as opaque).

User state stored in AVBuffer.opaque, handed to free and returned by av_buffer_get_opaque; never dereferenced by C. Owned by the buffer when free releases it (Rust: the leaked Box<T>), else borrowed for the buffer's life. Untouched on failure.

A new reference (refcount 1) to an av_mallocz'd AVBuffer over data, released by av_buffer_unref; NULL on allocation failure, with data, free and opaque untouched. Writable unless flags has AV_BUFFER_FLAG_READONLY. Rust: BufferReference::from_heap_vec / from_owner / from_read_only.

The buffer's data, an av_malloc-family block, released with av_free (NULL is a no-op). Installed as AVBuffer.free by buffer_create when no callback is given, and passed explicitly by av_buffer_alloc/av_buffer_realloc.
Unused: the AVBuffer free-callback signature's opaque, ignored by the body (av_buffer_alloc/realloc and buffer_create pass NULL).

Allocator stored in pool->alloc (NULL selects av_buffer_alloc) and called later by av_buffer_pool_get, under the pool mutex, from any thread, until the pool is freed (possibly after av_buffer_pool_uninit). Each result must be NULL or a sole, writable reference whose AVBuffer data holds at least size bytes. Rust: BufferPool::new passes NULL; custom allocators go through av_buffer_pool_init2 (BufferPool::with_allocator).

A fresh av_mallocz'd pool with an initialised mutex and refcount 1, the caller's reference, released by av_buffer_pool_uninit; NULL on allocation or mutex-init failure. Rust: adopted into BufferPoolBox = CBox<BufferPool, BufferPoolUninit>.

Allocator alloc2(opaque, size), called by av_buffer_pool_get under the pool mutex (serialized, any thread) whenever no free entry exists; NULL selects av_buffer_alloc. Results must be NULL or a sole, writable reference whose AVBuffer data holds at least size bytes, releasable by its own free callback on any thread.

User state stored in pool->opaque, passed to every alloc call and to pool_free(opaque) once the pool is actually freed (after av_buffer_pool_uninit and the return of every outstanding buffer). Ownership moves to the pool when pool_free is non-NULL and the call succeeds; on a NULL return pool_free is never called and the caller keeps it. Never dereferenced by C. Rust: a Box<F> leaked into the pool and dropped by the pool_free trampoline, or here when init2 fails.
Opaque releaser, called exactly once by buffer_pool_free on the thread releasing the pool's last reference, after every entry was flushed; never called on a failed init. May be NULL.
As av_buffer_pool_init: a fresh pool, refcount 1, released by av_buffer_pool_uninit; NULL on failure. Rust: BufferPoolBox.

The caller's AVBufferPool * slot (NULL slot and NULL pool are no-ops). Takes the caller's reference: NULLs the slot, flushes the free entries under the mutex, and drops one atomic reference; the pool body is freed (with pool_free(opaque)) now, or later by the last outstanding buffer's return. Rust: BufferPoolUninit's CDrop for BufferPoolBox passes a local slot holding the box's pointer.
A live reference, read only (struct copied by value); its AVBuffer's atomic_uint refcount is incremented (relaxed, unchecked: 2^32 leaked references wrap it). Never NULL: *buf is dereferenced.

A fresh av_mallocz'd AVBufferRef equal to *buf (same buffer, data, size), carrying the new counted reference; released by av_buffer_unref. NULL on allocation failure (count untouched). The struct is independent; the AVBuffer and its bytes are shared, writable by nobody while both references live (refcount >= 2). Rust: BufferUnref's CDupClone (BufferReferenceBox::clone/try_clone, BufferReferenceRef::try_clone), which refuses at a count of u32::MAX/2.

The caller's AVBufferRef * slot (NULL slot and NULL reference are no-ops). Consumes the reference: buffer_replace av_freep's the struct (NULLing the slot), then decrements AVBuffer.refcount (acq_rel); the last reference runs buffer->free(opaque, data) and av_free's the body unless BUFFER_FLAG_NO_FREE (pool entries, whose free is pool_release_buffer). Thread-safe per buffer.h. Rust: BufferUnref's CDrop for BufferReferenceBox passes a local slot holding the box's pointer.

Caller output buffer of buf_size bytes: av_bprint_init_for_buffer writes a NUL at buf[0] and av_bprintf writes the channel description (front left, ambisonic ACN <n>, user <n>, none, unknown, unused) truncated to fit with its NUL. As av_channel_name_bprint: an initialised AVBPrint borrowed mutably for the call, appended to with av_bprintf, not retained. Wrapped as Channel::append_description(self, &mut BPrintMut).

av_channel_from_string reads `str` during the call only (strncmp/strcmp against the static channel_names table, strtol for AMBI<n>/USR<n>; strtol's endptr is a local cursor into it); keeps no pointer. Dereferenced unconditionally, so NULL is UB (non-nullable). Wrapped as `&CStr`.

Read-only for the call, not retained. AMBISONIC order: reads nb_channels and u.mask only; highest_ambi = nb_channels - popcount(mask) - 1 and (order+1)*(order+1) are int arithmetic, which overflow for nb_channels near INT_MIN or highest_ambi >= 46340^2 (unreachable from safe paths; the wrapper answers None, C's EINVAL, before calling). CUSTOM order: walks the ids of nb_channels map elements with no NULL check (the wrapper refuses a NULL map or negative count). Any other order: EINVAL without reading more. Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::ambisonic_order -> Option<u32>.

Read-only for the call, not retained. idx is unsigned and compared with nb_channels converted to unsigned, so a negative count lets any idx through; CUSTOM order then reads u.map[idx] with no NULL check (out of bounds for a negative count). AMBISONIC/NATIVE read nb_channels and u.mask only. Returns the id by value (AV_CHAN_NONE for no channel; a map element may also hold AV_CHAN_NONE). Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::channel(usize) -> Option<Channel>, refusing a NULL map / negative custom count and indices beyond u32.

Read-only for the call, not retained: av_channel_layout_index_from_string then av_channel_layout_channel_from_index on the index found, so it inherits both contracts (CUSTOM map non-NULL with nb_channels elements; map names NUL-terminated when str holds '@' followed by text, since C strcmp's them). Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::channel_by_name -> Option<Channel>.

NUL-terminated channel name, read only during the call (strstr for '@', av_strlcpy of the abbreviation into a 16-byte local, strcmp against map names, av_channel_from_string); not retained. Non-NULL (C dereferences it). Rust: &CStr.

Read-only for the call, not retained. Reads nb_channels (<= 0 -> 0), the order, u.mask; CUSTOM checks u.map for NULL itself and then reads the ids of nb_channels elements. Safe for every state a safe path leaves. Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::is_valid -> bool.

First layout, read-only for the call, not retained; may alias chl1. Compares counts and orders, masks for two NATIVE or two AMBISONIC layouts, else av_channel_layout_channel_from_index for every index below the (equal) count, which dereferences a CUSTOM map with no NULL check. Returns 0 equal / 1 different (never negative in this revision). Rust: PartialEq for ChannelLayoutRef / ChannelLayout, false for a NULL-map custom layout without calling C.
Second layout: as chl.

Destination, borrowed exclusively for the call: uninitialised first (its old map freed), then overwritten with *src, and given a fresh av_malloc_array copy of src's map in CUSTOM order. On ENOMEM it is left CUSTOM with nb_channels set and a NULL map, which C readers would dereference: the wrapper resets it with av_channel_layout_uninit.

Source, borrowed read-only for the call; its map (CUSTOM order) is memcpy'd, nb_channels elements, and must be non-NULL when nb_channels > 0 (the wrapper refuses a NULL-map source before calling C). The opaque cookie is shallow-copied.

The layout to initialise, borrowed for the call; overwritten without uninit (order, nb_channels, u.map; opaque untouched), so a prior CUSTOM map leaks: the wrapper only passes a fresh zeroed value. Gains an av_calloc'd map of nb_channels AV_CHAN_UNKNOWN elements the layout owns; untouched on EINVAL/ENOMEM.

The layout to initialise, borrowed for the call; a copy of the first standard layout with nb_channels channels (all NATIVE, no map), or order UNSPEC with nb_channels set (u and opaque then untouched); never uninit first, so the wrapper only passes a fresh zeroed value.

Caller output buffer of buf_size bytes, initialised with av_bprint_init_for_buffer (NUL at buf[0], description truncated to fit with its NUL). NULL is allowed only with buf_size 0 (count-only); NULL with a nonzero size is EINVAL. buf_size is narrowed to unsigned. Not retained. Returns the needed size (len + 1), ERANGE when len >= INT_MAX. Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::write_description(&mut [u8]) (empty slice -> NULL, 0; length capped at u32::MAX) and description() -> CString, measuring first.
Read-only for the call, not retained: av_channel_layout_describe_bprint's contract (see there).

An initialised AVBPrint, borrowed mutably for the call only and not retained; C appends with av_bprintf / av_bprint_chars (truncating, never failing). Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::append_description(&self, BPrintMut) -> Result<(), i32>.

Read-only for the call, not retained. NATIVE: table lookup by mask, else '<n> channels (' + channel names via channel_from_index. CUSTOM: try_describe_ambisonic (av_channel_layout_ambisonic_order, map walk), has_channel_names / masked_description (map walks), else each channel's name and '@%s' of map[i].name, so every map name must be NUL-terminated and the map non-NULL with nb_channels elements. AMBISONIC: av_channel_layout_ambisonic_order (int arithmetic, see there) plus the non-diegetic mask as a native layout. UNSPEC: '<n> channels'. Unknown order: EINVAL. The wrapper refuses a NULL map, negative custom count, unterminated names and ambisonic counts C cannot compute an order of, with EINVAL, before calling.

The layout to initialise, borrowed for the call; order, nb_channels and u.mask overwritten without uninit (opaque untouched), so a prior CUSTOM map leaks: the wrapper only passes a fresh zeroed value. Untouched on EINVAL (mask 0). Allocates nothing.

The layout to initialise, borrowed for the call; overwritten without uninit (memset or a table copy), so a prior CUSTOM map leaks: the wrapper only passes a fresh zeroed value. May gain an owned map (parse_channel_list's av_dynarray2_add block, or av_calloc in the ambisonic path). On failure it is left in a state av_channel_layout_uninit accepts (no live map).

The layout description, a NUL-terminated string read during the call only (strcmp, av_strdup'd copy for parsing, strtol/strtoull). Not every string is a defined input: an `ambisonic <order>` segment whose order strtol narrows to exactly INT_MAX ("2147483647", "0x7fffffff", "-2147483649", ...; in the first segment or in one a `+` chains after a valid order) makes C's range check compute order + 1 and square it in int (channel_layout.c:341, :346), signed overflows, after which C returns 0 with an ambisonic layout of nb_channels 0. The wrapper (ChannelLayout::parse) mirrors strtol and refuses those descriptions with AVERROR(EINVAL) before the call (formats wave-3 batch-1 review). The other numeric paths saturate or narrow without overflow: the %d of av_sscanf, strtoull's mask (errno checked), strtol's count (`channels > 0`).

Read-only for the call, not retained. CUSTOM: walks the ids of nb_channels map elements with no NULL check. NATIVE/AMBISONIC: int nb_channels - popcount(mask), which overflows for a count near INT_MIN (unreachable from safe paths; refused by the wrapper), then popcount arithmetic; a NATIVE layout whose count is below its popcount can yield a negative non-error index (read as None). Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::index_of(Channel) -> Option<usize>.

Read-only for the call, not retained. CUSTOM: when str holds '@' followed by text, strcmp's it with each map name (names must be NUL-terminated) and compares ids; then, as for NATIVE/AMBISONIC, av_channel_from_string(str) and av_channel_layout_index_from_channel (see there). Other orders: EINVAL. Only EINVAL is returned on failure. Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::index_by_name -> Option<usize>, refusing unterminated names only when C would compare them.
NUL-terminated channel name, read only during the call; non-NULL. Rust: &CStr.

The layout to convert in place, borrowed exclusively for the call; the storage is the caller's (stack, embedded AVFrame/AVCodecContext.ch_layout, Rust CVal). C first rejects any layout av_channel_layout_check refuses (count <= 0, native count != popcount, custom map NULL or holding AV_CHAN_NONE, ambisonic count <= popcount, unknown order) with EINVAL, reading nb_channels map elements' ids. Lossy or impossible conversions return ENOSYS and custom_init failure ENOMEM, each leaving the layout untouched. On success it keeps opaque, and either uninits (freeing a custom u.map via av_freep) and rebuilds a mapless layout (unspec/native/ambisonic), or builds a fresh av_calloc map (custom target) that the layout then owns, released by av_channel_layout_uninit. Names are only tested by name[0], never strlen'd. Returns 0 (lossless or already in that order) or 1 (lossy). Rust: ChannelLayoutMut::retype / canonicalize on the exclusive handle.

Iteration state slot, read and written during the call (dereferenced unconditionally, so never NULL). *opaque is not a pointer to anything: C casts it to uintptr_t as the index of the next channel_layout_map entry (NULL starts at entry 0) and stores index+1 back while entries remain; past the end it leaves *opaque unchanged, so further calls keep returning NULL. Rust: the StandardLayouts iterator keeps the index as a usize and passes ptr::without_provenance_mut(index) in a local slot.

&channel_layout_map[i].layout, an entry of channel_layout.c's static const table: AV_CHANNEL_LAYOUT_* native layouts (mask, count = popcount) and AV_CHANNEL_LAYOUT_AMBISONIC_FIRST_ORDER, none in custom order, so no map; never written or freed. NULL past the last entry. Rust: Option<ChannelLayoutRef<'static>> as the iterator's item.

Read-only for the call. Rust: ChannelLayoutRef::subset, which answers 0 for a mapless custom layout without calling C.

The layout to dispose, borrowed for the call: frees u.map (av_freep) when order is CUSTOM and zeroes every field, opaque included. Accepts any layout C or the wrapper leaves (a zeroed one, a failed copy's NULL map). The storage itself is the caller's (stack, embedded field, Rust CVal).

Size string (an abbreviation from video_size_abbrs, or WxH read by two strtol calls with any one separator byte), read for the call only. Must not be NULL. strtol's long results narrow to int (implementation-defined, not UB): 4294967297x1 parses as 1x1.
Out-parameter, written only on success with a positive width, never read. Must not be NULL.

NULL for a value outside 0..AV_PIX_FMT_NB, else &av_pix_fmt_descriptors[fmt], an entry of pixdesc.c's static const table: immutable (name/alias string literals), never freed, process lifetime; entries for formats the table leaves out are all-zero (NULL name). Wrapped as PixelFormat::descriptor() -> Option<PixelFormatDescriptorRef<'static>>.

Never dereferenced: C only compares the address against the bounds of its static table and subtracts the base, returning AV_PIX_FMT_NONE for any pointer outside it (NULL and Rust-held copies included). Borrowed for the call only. Wrapped as PixelFormatDescriptorRef::pixel_format().

NULL starts the iteration (returns entry 0); otherwise must point into C's static descriptor table, since C does pointer arithmetic on it relative to the table and reads the following entries' names: a pointer to a copy is UB. Borrowed for the call. The Rust wrapper only passes NULL or a pointer av_pix_fmt_desc_get_id recognises.
NULL past the last named entry, else the next table entry with a non-NULL name (static, immutable, never freed).
h_shift: out-parameter, written with desc->log2_chroma_w when pix_fmt has a descriptor, untouched (AVERROR(ENOSYS)) otherwise. Not retained.
v_shift: out-parameter, written with desc->log2_chroma_h when pix_fmt has a descriptor, untouched (AVERROR(ENOSYS)) otherwise. Not retained.

log_ctx: read only by av_log when libavutil is built without CONFIG_PIXELUTILS (then it must be NULL or point to a struct led by a const AVClass *); with pixelutils (every crustify build) it is never read. Not retained. The Rust wrapper SadFn::new passes NULL.

Function pointer into libavutil's static sad_c table or an x86 SIMD routine (chosen by av_get_cpu_flags and aligned 0/1/2); never freed, valid for the process. NULL when w_bits/h_bits are outside 1..=5 or differ (only square blocks), or without CONFIG_PIXELUTILS. Wrapped as pixelutils::SadFn (Copy, Send, Sync).

src1: a 2-D block of (1<<bits)x(1<<bits) bytes read row by row, rows `stride1` apart (stride may be negative or smaller than the width); read only during the call. SIMD variants (x86 sad_a_/sad_u_) require src1 aligned to the block size when the getter was asked for aligned >= 1 (mova faults otherwise).
src2: same block shape as src1 with rows `stride2` apart; aligned to the block size required only for aligned == 2 (x86 sad_a_). Read only during the call.
Caller buffer of len bytes, write-only (fread from /dev/urandom on this build); fully written on success, possibly partly on failure. Not retained. Must be valid even for len 0 (passed to fread).
Fresh full-size zero-filled av_malloc-family C allocation; sole ownership transfers to caller, av_free is paired release. Opaque hash/cipher allocators need init before operations.
Call-scoped bytes; C retains no pointer. Exact length is determined by the count or supported digest/key size.
Entirely ignored, including null, by the current implementation.
Exclusively borrowed full initialized context; no suballocations or retained input pointers.
Call-scoped input bytes or NULL to generate keystream; exact overlap with dst supported.
Nonempty byte key; C requires a multiple-of-eight key bit count and reads at most first 256 key bytes. Empty/negative C lengths are unsafe and excluded.
Exclusive full-size storage, initialized in place with no reads of the previous state; no pointer retained.
An AVPixFmtDescriptor borrowed shared for the call only and never retained: C's own static table entry (av_pix_fmt_desc_get) or a caller-built descriptor. As av_read_image_line2.

Caller output array of w uint16_t written during the call only; forwards to av_read_image_line2 with element size 2. Read-only image planes uint8_t *data[4] and linesize[4] are array params wavefront does not record: C reads data[comp.plane] rows and, with read_pal_component, data[1] as a palette indexed 4*val + c.

An AVPixFmtDescriptor borrowed shared for the call only and never retained: C's own static table entry (av_pix_fmt_desc_get) or a caller-built descriptor. Only comp[c] and flags are read; c must be 0..4, and comp[c]'s depth/shift/offset/step drive shifts and pointer walks the wrapper validates before calling.

Caller output array of w elements of dst_element_size bytes (4: uint32_t, otherwise uint16_t), written during the call only; type-erased, wrapped generically over a sealed u16/u32 element trait. Read-only image planes uint8_t *data[4] and linesize[4] are array params wavefront does not record: C reads data[comp.plane] rows and, with read_pal_component, data[1] as a palette indexed 4*val + c.
Old block, ownership taken: realloc(ptr, size + !size). On failure (NULL return) the old block is NOT freed and stays owned by the caller. Only malloc alignment (16 on glibc x86_64), not ALIGN.

Resized block; NULL on failure or size > max_alloc_size. realloc-style: releases and reallocates the same slot, so not a constructor (schema); no lifecycle role. The raw-lifetime void tier binds av_free/av_malloc*/av_memdup instead.

Old block, ownership taken on success: av_realloc(ptr, nmemb*size) after an overflow check. On failure (overflow, max_alloc, or realloc failure) returns NULL and the old block is untouched and still the caller's. NULL allocates.
Resized block of nmemb*size bytes (1 byte for 0), malloc alignment only (max_align_t), not ALIGN; NULL on failure. realloc-style, so no constructor role; released by av_free.
Old block, ownership always taken: resized on success, av_free'd on failure (size overflow or allocation failure). NULL allocates.
Resized block of nelem*elsize bytes (1 for 0), malloc alignment; NULL on failure, the input then freed. Released by av_free. realloc-style, no constructor role.

Declared void* but a T** slot (memcpy'd), borrowed and non-NULL. The pointee's ownership transfers in and back out: size 0 av_freep()s it (slot NULL, returns 0); on success the slot holds the resized block; on failure the old block is freed, the slot set NULL, AVERROR(ENOMEM) returned. A NULL pointee allocates.

Declared void* but a T** slot (memcpy'd), borrowed and non-NULL. The pointee goes through av_realloc_f: on success the slot holds the resized block of nmemb*size bytes (1 byte for 0); on failure the old block is freed, the slot set NULL, and AVERROR(ENOMEM) returned unless nmemb or size is 0. A NULL pointee allocates.
Out-parameter, written once, never read. Must not be NULL.
Out-parameter, written once, never read. Must not be NULL. C overflows (UB) negating a result term of INT_MIN, reachable with max > INT_MAX or negative, and FFABS(INT64_MIN) of num/den.

Forwarded unchanged to av_refstruct_alloc_ext_c. free_cb(opaque, obj) is stored in the object's RefCount header and called once, by whichever thread's av_refstruct_unref drops the last reference, with the payload obj (exclusively reached, fully initialised by then) just before the block is av_free'd; it must dispose of what obj owns but not free obj. NULL: no callback. Never called if the allocation fails. Rust: release_with::<T, F> trampoline running a boxed FnOnce(T::Mut) + Send + 'static (alloc_with_release).

User opaque, wrapped as (AVRefStructOpaque){.nc = opaque} and stored in the object header; never dereferenced by C, only passed back to free_cb once. Ownership of what it points to moves to the object's release when free_cb consumes it (Rust: the leaked Box<F> of alloc_with_release, dropped by release_with); on a NULL return the caller keeps it.

As av_refstruct_alloc_ext_c, which this static inline forwards to. NULL when size + REFCOUNT_OFFSET overflows or av_malloc fails; otherwise the payload of a fresh RefStruct object (header refcount 1, payload aligned to >= 16) the caller owns, released by av_refstruct_unref and shared by av_refstruct_ref/_c. Zeroed unless flags has AV_REFSTRUCT_FLAG_NO_ZEROING (then uninitialised). Rust: RefStructBox<T> from alloc_with_release (zeroed, with release) or the CAlloc impl of RefStructUnref (NO_ZEROING, no callback, new_uninit/assume_init).

free_cb(opaque, obj) is stored in the object's RefCount header and called once, by whichever thread's av_refstruct_unref drops the last reference, with the payload obj (exclusively reached, fully initialised by then) just before the block is av_free'd; it must dispose of what obj owns but not free obj. NULL: no callback. Never called if the allocation fails. Rust: release_with::<T, F> trampoline running a boxed FnOnce(T::Mut) + Send + 'static (alloc_with_release).

NULL when size + REFCOUNT_OFFSET overflows or av_malloc fails; otherwise the payload of a fresh RefStruct object (header refcount 1, payload aligned to >= 16) the caller owns, released by av_refstruct_unref and shared by av_refstruct_ref/_c. Zeroed unless flags has AV_REFSTRUCT_FLAG_NO_ZEROING (then uninitialised). Rust: RefStructBox<T> from alloc_with_release (zeroed, with release) or the CAlloc impl of RefStructUnref (NO_ZEROING, no callback, new_uninit/assume_init).

Static inline: av_refstruct_alloc_ext_c(size, 0, {NULL}, NULL). Returns a zeroed object of `size` bytes after a REFCOUNT_OFFSET header in one av_malloc block, holding one counted reference the caller releases with av_refstruct_unref (no free_cb, so the payload is never finalized). NULL when size + REFCOUNT_OFFSET overflows or av_malloc fails (av_max_alloc). Aligned to at least 16.
obj is a live RefStruct object (never NULL); C acquire-loads the header's count and returns whether it is 1.

A new pool holding one RefStruct reference (header refcount 1), released by av_refstruct_pool_uninit (av_refstruct_unref) and shareable with av_refstruct_ref. NULL on allocation or mutex-init failure. No callbacks: equivalent to av_refstruct_pool_alloc_ext(size, flags, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL), so RESET/FREE_ON_INIT_ERROR are filtered out and only NO_ZEROING / ZERO_EVERY_TIME take effect.

free_cb(opaque): called once by pool_free, after the mutex is destroyed, when the last pool reference and the last outstanding entry are gone; not called when alloc fails (mutex-init failure av_frees the pool directly). Rust: free_with trampoline dropping the boxed PoolState.

free_entry_cb(opaque, obj): called on each entry freed after the pool is uninited (refstruct_pool_uninit's flush, or pool_return_entry after uninit), outside the mutex; also on init failure with FREE_ON_INIT_ERROR. Rust: free_entry_with trampoline.

init_cb(opaque, obj) -> int: stored in the pool; called by av_refstruct_pool_get (outside the pool mutex, on the getting thread) on each newly allocated entry, zeroed unless NO_ZEROING/ZERO_EVERY_TIME; <0 fails the get (entry av_free'd after the optional reset/free_entry callbacks). Rust: init_with trampoline (zeroes the entry first under ZERO_EVERY_TIME).

User opaque, wrapped as {.nc = opaque} and stored in pool->opaque; passed to every callback and to free_cb once when the pool is freed; never dereferenced by C. Rust: the leaked Box<PoolState<T,S>> dropped by free_with; kept by the caller on a NULL return.

reset_cb(opaque, obj): installed as each entry's RefStruct free_cb (pool_reset_entry), so it runs on whichever thread drops an entry's last reference, before the entry is relinked or freed; also on init failure with RESET_ON_INIT_ERROR. Rust: reset_with trampoline.

As av_refstruct_pool_alloc_ext_c, which this static inline forwards to. NULL on allocation or mutex-init failure; otherwise a new pool (itself a RefStruct object, refcount 1) the caller owns, released by av_refstruct_pool_uninit and shared with av_refstruct_ref. Callbacks run on any thread, concurrently. NO_ZEROING is copied to entry_flags, RESET/FREE_ON_INIT_ERROR are filtered without their callbacks, ZERO_EVERY_TIME forces entry NO_ZEROING. Rust: TypedRefStructPool<T>::with_callbacks (RefStructPoolArc inside; NO_ZEROING stripped so entries are valid T).

free_cb(opaque): called once by pool_free, after the mutex is destroyed, when the last pool reference and the last outstanding entry are gone; not called when alloc fails (mutex-init failure av_frees the pool directly). Rust: free_with trampoline dropping the boxed PoolState.

free_entry_cb(opaque, obj): called on each entry freed after the pool is uninited (refstruct_pool_uninit's flush, or pool_return_entry after uninit), outside the mutex; also on init failure with FREE_ON_INIT_ERROR. Rust: free_entry_with trampoline.

init_cb(opaque, obj) -> int: stored in the pool; called by av_refstruct_pool_get (outside the pool mutex, on the getting thread) on each newly allocated entry, zeroed unless NO_ZEROING/ZERO_EVERY_TIME; <0 fails the get (entry av_free'd after the optional reset/free_entry callbacks). Rust: init_with trampoline (zeroes the entry first under ZERO_EVERY_TIME).

reset_cb(opaque, obj): installed as each entry's RefStruct free_cb (pool_reset_entry), so it runs on whichever thread drops an entry's last reference, before the entry is relinked or freed; also on init failure with RESET_ON_INIT_ERROR. Rust: reset_with trampoline.

NULL on allocation or mutex-init failure; otherwise a new pool (itself a RefStruct object, refcount 1) the caller owns, released by av_refstruct_pool_uninit and shared with av_refstruct_ref. Callbacks run on any thread, concurrently. NO_ZEROING is copied to entry_flags, RESET/FREE_ON_INIT_ERROR are filtered without their callbacks, ZERO_EVERY_TIME forces entry NO_ZEROING. Rust: TypedRefStructPool<T>::with_callbacks (RefStructPoolArc inside; NO_ZEROING stripped so entries are valid T).

A live pool the caller holds a reference to (UB after av_refstruct_pool_uninit drops the last one); C locks pool->mutex around the free list, bumps pool->refcount atomically and may call init_cb. Not retained by the caller's pointer: the returned entry keeps its own pointer to the pool (ref->opaque) and a count in pool->refcount, so the entry outlives the caller's reference.

NULL on ENOMEM or init_cb failure; otherwise an entry (a RefStruct object of pool->size bytes with refcount 1) the caller owns, released by av_refstruct_unref, which runs reset_cb and returns it to the pool (or frees it after uninit). Its bytes depend on the pool's flags: under AV_REFSTRUCT_POOL_FLAG_ZERO_EVERY_TIME every entry, new or reused, is memset to zero right before it is returned, after init_cb or the last reset_cb (refstruct.c refstruct_pool_get_ext; new entries are then allocated with NO_ZEROING, so init_cb sees uninitialised bytes); otherwise a reused entry holds what its last user and reset_cb left, and a new one is zeroed before init_cb unless NO_ZEROING (then uninitialised apart from what init_cb wrote). Rust: TypedRefStructPool<T>::get -> Option<RefStructBox<T>> (NO_ZEROING stripped; init_with zeroes a new entry first under ZERO_EVERY_TIME).

`*poolp` is NULL (no-op) or one counted reference to a pool, which the call releases and NULLs. Static inline over av_refstruct_unref(poolp): the last reference runs refstruct_pool_uninit (marks the pool uninited, frees the free list's entries through free_entry_cb) and pool_unref; the struct itself is freed only once every outstanding entry has also been returned (pool_return_entry), so entries may outlive the last pool reference.

obj is a live RefStruct object (never NULL: get_refcount reads the header before it). Only the bookkeeping header at obj - REFCOUNT_OFFSET is written (relaxed atomic increment); the user data is untouched.
Returns obj itself, now carrying one more counted reference the caller owns and must release with av_refstruct_unref.
As av_refstruct_ref, for a const reference: C casts const away only to increment the bookkeeping header's atomic count, never touching the user data.
Returns obj as a const reference the caller owns (one more count) and releases with av_refstruct_unref; the holder must not write the user data through it.

dstp is a slot (void * standing for T **) holding NULL or an owned reference. If *dstp == src nothing happens; otherwise the old reference is released (av_refstruct_unref) and a new reference to src (av_refstruct_ref_c), or NULL, is stored. The slot is borrowed for the call.
src is NULL or a live RefStruct object the caller keeps its own reference to; C up-refs it into *dstp (const cast away in the stored slot).

objp is a slot (void * standing for T **): C memcpy-reads the object pointer from it, writes NULL back, then drops one counted reference of the object (free_cb then ref->free when the count hits zero). The slot itself is borrowed for the call; the reference it held is consumed. A NULL *objp is a no-op; objp itself must not be NULL.

In/out state slot holding one int64_t timestamp in fs_tb units (AV_NOPTS_VALUE before the first call): read, then overwritten on every return path; never stored past the call. Must not be NULL (dereferenced unconditionally).

Exclusively borrowed full initialized context; no suballocations or retained input pointers.
Call-scoped writable output: maximum digest is 40 bytes (RIPEMD), 32 (SHA), 64 (SHA512). Only active digest prefix is written.
Exclusive full-size storage, initialized in place with no reads of the previous state; no pointer retained.
Exclusively borrowed full initialized context; no suballocations or retained input pointers.
Call-scoped readable len-byte input, never stored. Empty slices use nonnull pointers.

Caller array of planar ? nb_channels : 1 plane slots (C writes that many). On success slot 0 owns one av_malloc block of the returned size (release: av_freep(&audio_data[0]) / av_free), and slots 1.. borrow it at i * linesize. Each plane's first nb_samples * block_align bytes are set to silence (0x80 for U8/U8P, else 0); the alignment padding stays uninitialised. Untouched on failure (the block is freed). Wrapped as samplefmt::SampleBuffer::new.
Optional out-param, the aligned plane size; written on success.

Out-slot: on success an av_calloc array of planar ? nb_channels : 1 plane pointers, owned by the caller (av_freep(audio_data)), whose slot 0 owns the av_malloc sample block (av_freep(&(*audio_data)[0])) as av_samples_alloc fills it. On failure *audio_data is NULL (av_freep). A negative nb_channels makes av_calloc fail (ENOMEM) for planar formats before validation. Wrapped as samplefmt::SampleBufferWithPointers::new.
Optional out-param, the aligned plane size; written on success.

planar ? nb_channels : 1 plane pointers; each plane written for nb_samples * block_align bytes at dst_offset * block_align. Not retained. memcpy unless |dst[0] - src[0]| < data_size (offsets ignored), then memmove: copies within one buffer go through memmove only when plane 0 of dst and src coincide closely. All products are int (overflow UB for unchecked counts).
planar ? nb_channels : 1 plane pointers read for nb_samples * block_align bytes at src_offset * block_align; may be the same array as dst (memmove path). Not retained.

Caller array of plane pointers: on success C zeroes planar ? nb_channels : 1 slots, then (buf non-NULL) sets slot i to buf + i * linesize. The elements borrow buf; the array itself is not retained. Untouched on failure.

Sample buffer, never dereferenced: only offset into audio_data (const cast away, so callers write through the slots). Must hold the returned size, else the plane pointers are computed past its end (pointer arithmetic UB). NULL only computes size and linesize and zeroes the slots.
Optional out-param, the av_samples_get_buffer_size linesize; written on success.

Optional out-param: the aligned bytes per plane (planar) or of the single packed plane; written only on success. Validation guarantees nb_channels * nb_samples * bytes <= INT_MAX - align * nb_channels, so every later int product is in range; negative align always fails (INT_MAX / align <= 0 < nb_channels). A non-power-of-two align is accepted and FFALIGN then rounds to a non-multiple, still >= the data size. C defect: with align 0 the range check admits nb_samples == INT_MAX - 31, and FFALIGN(nb_samples, 32) computes nb_samples + 32 first (signed overflow, UBSan samplefmt.c:137); that count is already a multiple of 32, so the Rust wrappers pass align 1 for it (c_align), the same layout. Every other input is UB-free (5M-input edge fuzz under UBSan).

planar ? nb_channels : 1 plane pointers; each plane memset for nb_samples * block_align bytes at offset * block_align (0x80 for U8/U8P, 0 otherwise). Not retained; int products overflow for unchecked counts.

Not touched when opts is NULL or empty. Each value reaches C UB exactly as av_opt_set's val does (see there). Wrapped as the safe opt::ObjectMut::set_options_string (options wave-0 batch-1 review), which refuses a list holding any such value before C runs.

Set of pair separator bytes (strspn), read for the call only. Must not be NULL.

struct tm whose integer fields named by the format are written (also before a later mismatch); tm_zone untouched. Wrapped as bprint::TmMut.
Format string, read for the call; a trailing % reads the NUL and fails before reading further.
Input string, read up to its NUL at most; the returned pointer points into it.
NULL on mismatch, else a suffix of p (first unread byte or its NUL), borrowed from p: Option<&'s CStr>.

Format, read for the call only; its conversions decide the type and count of the variadic destinations (int sizes by hh/h/l/ll/j/z/t, float/double, byte buffers for c/s/[, void* for p). Width digits overflow int (UB); %s/%[ without width and %ms write unbounded; positional %n$ is supported via arg_n.
Input, read for the call only through a fake FILE (memchr up to the NUL). Must not be NULL.
Read for the call only, up to the first difference or NUL. Must not be NULL.
Read for the call only. Must not be NULL.
Source string, read up to its NUL (strlen + memcpy) for the call only; any allocator. NULL is accepted and yields NULL.

Fresh av_realloc(NULL, strlen(s) + 1) block holding a NUL-terminated copy of s (deep clone), released by av_free. NULL when s is NULL, when strlen(s) + 1 exceeds av_max_alloc (INT_MAX by default; a string of exactly the limit's length already fails), or on allocation failure. Not av_malloc-aligned (av_realloc).
Caller buffer of errbuf_size bytes, written with a NUL-terminated (truncated) description via av_strlcpy/strerror_r/snprintf; nothing written when errbuf_size is 0. Not retained.

Needle, matched case-insensitively (av_stristr), read for the call only. Must not be NULL (strlen). An empty `from` loops forever (av_stristr matches it at the same position without advancing); the Rust wrapper returns a copy of `str` instead.
Haystack, read for the call only. Must not be NULL.
Replacement, read for the call only. Must not be NULL (strlen).

Fresh NUL-terminated string from av_bprint_finalize (av_malloc / av_realloc storage, or av_memdup of the internal buffer); released by av_free. NULL when the AVBPrint ran out of memory (incomplete) or finalize fails.
Read for the call only. Must not be NULL.

Optional out-slot; on a match receives a pointer into str just past the prefix (borrowed from str). Untouched otherwise. (C writes the slot itself; its char pointee is const, so `mutable` is false per the schema.)
Read for the call only. Must not be NULL.
Haystack, read for the call only. Must not be NULL.
Needle, read for the call only. Must not be NULL; empty matches at s1.
Pointer into s1 at the first case-insensitive match (const cast away; callers must not write), or NULL.

Destination buffer of `size` bytes holding a NUL-terminated string, borrowed for the call: strlen(dst) is taken WITHOUT a bound, so a buffer with no NUL within size is overread (the safe wrapper rejects it). When size <= strlen(dst) + 1 nothing is written; otherwise av_strlcpy appends at dst + len within size. [Symbol: Returns strlen(dst) + strlen(src) (differs from BSD strlcat when size <= strlen(dst)). No allocation or retention.]
Source string, read up to its NUL for the call only. Must not be NULL.

Destination buffer of `size` bytes holding a NUL-terminated string (unbounded strlen, as av_strlcat); vsnprintf appends within size - len bytes (none when size <= len). [Symbol: Returns strlen(dst) + the untruncated formatted length; a vsnprintf failure (text > INT_MAX) adds (size_t)-1. The safe wrapper formats in Rust and passes it through %s.]
printf format, read for the call; the variadic arguments follow it. Must not be NULL.

Destination buffer of `size` bytes, borrowed for the call: at most size-1 bytes of src are copied and a NUL written unless size is 0 (then nothing is written, so dst may be any pointer). Bytes after the NUL are untouched. [Symbol: Returns strlen(src); a result >= size means truncation. No allocation or retention.]
Source string, read up to its NUL (strlen for the return) for the call only. Must not be NULL.

String compared, read in step with b up to the first NUL of either, a difference, or n bytes. Must not be NULL. [Symbol: Returns the difference of the last compared bytes after ASCII lowercasing, as uint8_t; 0 when n is 0.]
String compared, as a.

Source bytes, read for the call only: memchr scans at most len bytes for a NUL and the copy stops there, so s is a NUL-terminated string or any buffer of at least len readable bytes (callers pass sub-ranges of larger strings: get_extension, parse_cookie). NULL is accepted and yields NULL.

Fresh av_realloc(NULL, n + 1) block, n = min(len, offset of the first NUL), holding those n bytes plus a NUL (deep clone of a prefix), released by av_free. NULL when s is NULL, n + 1 exceeds av_max_alloc, or allocation fails.
Bytes read up to the first NUL or len bytes, whichever first: any buffer of at least len readable bytes, or a shorter NUL-terminated string. Header inline.

Searched buffer: memcmp windows of strlen(needle) bytes ending within hay_length bytes, read regardless of NULs, so it must have hay_length readable bytes (not merely a string). Not read when needle is empty or longer than hay_length.
Searched-for string, read (strlen, memcmp) for the call only. Must not be NULL.
Address of the first match inside haystack (haystack itself for an empty needle), const cast away; NULL when there is none. Writing through it would write the caller's const haystack.
Prefix, read up to its NUL or a mismatch. Must not be NULL.

Optional out slot, written only on a match with the address in str just past the prefix (a borrow of str). NULL discards it. (The slot itself is written; mutable is false because the innermost pointee, char, is const.)
